goal.title: Goal and requirements
goal.why: NASA starts every mission from the end product and turns it into measurable requirements; each decision later is checked against them.
goal.sources: Mass margin: GSFC-STD-1000 Gold Rules, Table 1.06-1 (Pre-Phase A).
goal.conflict: Resources are shared, so the roles pull in different directions — there is no single perfect design.

roles.planner: Orbit, launcher and ground stations. Answers for budget, comms and schedule.
roles.scientist: Instruments. Answers for the data that reaches Earth.
roles.engineer: Solar arrays, battery, radio, computer, attitude control and engine. Answers for power.
roles.designer: The bus, which side each part faces and the mass margin. Answers for mass and the fit in the fairing.

concept.hint: Higher orbits live longer and see stations longer, but the radio is weaker and launchers lift less.

flight.soon: The flight on a map of the Earth comes with task 010. You can open the report already.

report.soon: The full report with simulation, causal chains and scores comes with task 011. For now — the checks of your design.
report.ready: No failed checks — the design is ready for launch.

credits.title: Credits

credits.noLogo: NASA logos and insignia are not used. Every formula and number in the game links to its NASA document.
